notes: The schematic image was not available; wiring follows the standard Arduino MKR GSM 1400 NeoPixel level-shifter circuit described in the text: 2N7000 source to the Arduino data pin, gate to 3.3V (VCC), drain to NeoPixel DIN with a 10k pull-up to 5V.
The data pin is assumed to be D6; the text does not name it.
The catalogue led-ring entry has no ports, so DIN, PWR and GND are used as informal port names on ring1 for the wire connections.
The 2N7000 pin order (S, G, D) is assumed as TO-92 pins 1, 2, 3. It sits in columns 10, 11 and 12 of the top half of the breadboard.
The resistor is a catalogue 'resistor' with value=10k, even though the catalogue label says 100 ohm.
The tutorial uses a single NeoPixel in the layout; the ring is used here as listed in the parts.

Connections between the board and the antenna, SIM card, battery and USB cable have no named ports because the catalogue board entry has no ports for them. The battery is connected through its JST connector.
The Arduino 5V pin supplies the NeoPixel and the pull-up resistor.
The rail holes tp.1, tp.2 and tp.12 are the + rail. tn.1 and tn.2 are the - rail.
